Kevin Sealy (5/5): This was incredibly cool to see. We stopped to see the Northern part of Yellowstone while traveling through Montana. Everything about Mammoth Hot Springs was great. If you are trying to decide what to do while at Yellowstone this should be high on the list. | vasista k.j (5/5): An Otherworldly and Unforgettable Stop in Yellowstone

Mammoth Hot Springs is an absolutely stunning and surreal destination that feels unlike anything else in Yellowstone National Park. The terraced limestone formations, with their vibrant, constantly changing colors and steaming vents, create a truly otherworldly landscape that is a must-see stop for anyone visiting the park. It's full of geothermal beauty and geologic wonder.

To truly appreciate the full beauty of the springs, you have to get out of your car and explore the upper and lower boardwalks. The Upper Terrace Drive is also highly recommended, as it's a short loop that provides incredible views and access to beautiful spots. For those who want to do the full hike, a great tip is to start at the top and work your way down, which makes the trip back to the car much easier. The hike is worth it, as the views are outstanding and varied. This place is always changing, making each visit a unique experience.

Beyond the springs, the nearby town of Mammoth adds to the charm of the area. With its beautiful old buildings and elk often roaming around, the town has a welcoming, small-town feel. It's a convenient and scenic stop to round out your visit. As a final tip, be sure to try the huckleberry fudge ice cream in the dining room—it's a delicious way to cap off the experience. | Brian Ingle (5/5): Mammoth hot springs was one of our gorgeous Destination stops. The Museum of the Rockies is a perfect activity for anyone visiting Bozeman, especially if you’re short on time. This beautiful museum is a must-see for dinosaur lovers, featuring a vast collection of impressive, well-maintained dinosaur skeletons and engaging exhibits.

Beyond the incredible dinosaur displays, the museum also offers a variety of other attractions. You can relax and enjoy a show at the comfortable, small planetarium for a nominal price. I visited the Four Corners Monument and it was such a fun and unique stop. The drive in is beautiful from any direction, and there are clear signs leading to the entrance. I bought my ticket at the gate and parked right next to the site — plenty of parking and clean public restrooms.

Emily Goodin (4/5): This concert venue is inside "Centre Church". The Google Maps placement pin was in the road so I didn't realize that the "Performing Arts" venue was inside the (mega)church building until I checked the address when setting up a Lyft ride.

*Important Note!* Cell phone coverage somehow dropped to nothing right inside the door! I previously had perfect reception for Google Maps, Lyft rides, and the ZipBy parking app. YMMV but for me it was quite annoying. Accessing my Ticketmaster tickets was quite problematic until the usher let me use a wifi hotspot she had previously set up on her phone. (Huge kudos to the usher!)  I've always had perfect reception at other theaters in Vancouver (Vogue, Hollywood, QE, Pearl, etc) so I didn't do that. I recommend downloading your tickets to Google/Apple wallet beforehand. Lesson learned!

Anyway, as for the auditorium itself, we saw Gogo Penguin there and we were very happy with the concert. The distance between rows was a squeeze for my 195cm tall husband, but there was an empty seat next to us so he could splay his legs enough to make do. The associated lighting effects were a bit dated/amateurish (not sure who was in charge of that) but the music and acoustics were fine for this genre (jazz with some electronic elements). It's nice that some light snacks were on offer in the lobby. I parked at the nearby EasyPark 129 (Queen Eliz Theater) because I had parked there before and the ZipBy app works well for me.

I'm not keen on a religious entity making money from my ticket purchase, but if other artists that are favorites of mine were performing at The Centre, without another nearby option, I would consider going back. | Patrick Graham (4/5): After eating an amazing dinner at Cactus Club, we came here to see Jann Arden in concert. The seats were really good but they did not seem to have any air conditioning, which made the evening not quite as enjoyable. It was summer and very hot and humid. Hopefully for future events they fix that.

Jann Arden put on an amazing performance! She was playing all these covers from her new album along with some of her own hit songs. She had funny stories she told between songs and she could be a comedienne.

Here was her set list:
I Would Die For You
Time For Mercy
Will You Remember Me
One Of Us
Could I Be Your Girl
Insensitive
Unloved
Crazy
The Sound Of
You Gotta Be
Wicked Game
Good Mother

The music and sound was great! It is a good venue for a concert but they need to make the temperature more comfortable inside. | Lucy Yep. Agatka Hohatka (5/5): Beautiful palace with stunning architecture and atmosphere. I highly recommend buying the ticket to the Royal Apartments (book well in advance). Very crowded, but the gardens with peacocks are amazing. Beautiful interiors, lots of details to admire. Definitely worth visiting and the ticket price. | Mike C (5/5): The Real Alcázar of Seville is one of those rare places where the exterior beauty only hints at the wonders waiting inside. From the moment you approach the palace, the outside already sets the tone—strong Moorish walls, elegant archways, and lush gardens stretching out like an invitation to step into a different century.

But it’s once you cross the threshold that the real magic begins. Inside, the palace feels like a living tapestry of cultures. The intricate tilework, carved wooden ceilings, and peaceful courtyards all blend Moorish artistry with later Christian influences in a way that feels harmonious rather than contrasted. The Patio de las Doncellas is a highlight—its reflective pool and delicate arches make it feel like stepping into a dream. And if you wander deeper, the rooms reveal layer after layer of history, from royal chambers to salons decorated with impossibly detailed azulejos.

The gardens outside are just as impressive as the interiors. They’re spacious, fragrant, and full of hidden corners—from fountains to shaded pathways and even peacocks wandering freely. It’s easy to spend as much time outdoors as you do inside, especially if you love photography or simply enjoy soaking in tranquil scenery.

Overall, the Real Alcázar marries exterior grandeur with interior artistry in a way that few places can match. Whether you’re admiring its fortress-like facade or getting lost in its ornate rooms and gardens, it’s a palace that leaves a lasting impression. | Caitlin Bones (4/5): Definitely buy tickets in advance and as far in advance as possible if you want to do the upstairs state rooms. Fabulous site that is a definite must visit on any trip and I recommend visiting early morning though it is busy all day - you can easily fill multiple hours at the site.

I’ve removed one star as gardens were closed when I visited due to a storm (Storm Leonardo) which is understandable in some ways but therefore €39.90 tickets felt expensive when half of it was unavailable - I think a partial refund could have been offered as a gesture of good will as not a single part of the gardens were open.

Indoors is breath-taking beautiful and no photos can do it justice.

​The Shopping:
We were surprised by the variety. We spent a lot of time in the collectible stores and even found a few impressive shops dedicated to motorcycle gear, carrying everything from helmets to high-quality leather wear. If you’re a hobbyist or a rider, there’s plenty to see. We also stumbled upon a fantastic store for baking and cooking products that had everything you could need for a home kitchen.
​The Food & Finds:
You can’t go to Columbus without hitting the Amish Market. The bakery side was packed, but we waited in line for the homemade pretzels—fresh, warm, and absolutely worth the wait! We also found a great discount store that had chips, cookies, and snacks at amazing prices, which was perfect for the kids.
​The Layout:

Ryan Davis (4/5): Grabbed lunch here with some friends the other day. Schmidt's comes with a lot of hype. I'm not sure it totally lives up to it in certain ways.

I decided to do something I never do, I ordered the buffet. I wanted to try a lot of different things, and the buffet seemed to make the most sense.

The buffet was solid. The mashed potatoes and gravy were delicious. The macaroni and cheese was super creamy. And the sausage stew was one of the best stews I've ever had. That's the one thing I would highly recommend.

I also ordered a vanilla cream puff to go. I wasn't impressed. Maybe it's not a dessert for me, but I just didn't like it very much.

high bank distillery co::columbus.query: High Bank Distillery Co, Columbus, United States
high bank distillery co::columbus.google_reviews_summary:
Hari Karunakaran (4/5): This is my dinner experience at High Bank distillery, Grandview, Columbus

Drinks first! It’s a distillery after all. The bourbons were smooth and had great notes. I will save the technical notes for the qualified. I recommend getting a bourbon flight and do the default list on the menu or choose other options. I had about 5 different 1 oz pours and they were all great bourbons. Definitely underestimated and under appreciated bourbons.

Food tasted and reviewed:
Sticky chicken wings (Gochujang and BBQ)
Deviled eggs
Elote dip
Burrata
Margarita pizza

Taste profile: 4.5/5
We started with the thin crust pizza. It’s a perfect crispy, right sized, aptly topped flatbread. Perfect nibbler in between a sip of the bourbons.
The deviled eggs were delicious and tempting us to order some more. I love it when the acid and fat are well balanced. Well done with the plating too.
Sticky chicken wings (bone-in) were tender and can easily be had with a fork and knife. Nothing to mess with specially since I didn’t see the wet wipes provided.
Elote dip - just dull and plain. Nothing to write about. Let’s skip it.
Burrata stole the night for me. Creamy, fresh and delicious cheese with generous side of crisp toasted bread and onion jam(?) was amazing. Thats a go-to starter for me next time.

Overall, a spirited (pun intended), delightful and tasteful experience.

Cuisine: American

Overall Quality: 4.75/5
Food was fresh and mostly seemed cooked from scratch.

Decor: industrial looking decor, regular tables and high tables. Good for office parties, business and casual dining.

Ambience: quiet yet mildly noisy. Pleasant atmosphere with a quiet view of the distillery enhances the dining experience.

Friendliness: the staff were friendly and welcoming.

Overall, High Bank Distillery is a must try for any occasion or a casual drink or dinner kind of night. There is plenty of good food and room for everyone. A repeat destination for me. | Stephanie Cotter (5/5): We visited the restaurant on a Saturday evening. We made a reservation but there were several open tables when we arrived. The restaurant offers indoor and outdoor seating. The only challenge is parking.

We got a flight of 4 and enjoyed every pour. This was our first time visiting so we were unaware the Whiskey War Double Double is a limited release. We would have loved to bought that bottle!

My BLT salad was delicious and my husband enjoyed his burger. The fries were crispy and absolutely perfect. Our server was friendly, prompt, and patient. She also made a recommendation to add an additional pour to our flight and we were not disappointed. We would absolutely go back. | Ryan (Rye105) (3/5): Went with some friends today. The food was mediocre. It was lacking a little seasoning. The avocado toast was missing some pepper, honestly some sea salt would have been good in it as well. The breakfast burrito had actual potato half’s in it that made it awkward to eat and wasn’t seasoned. The nachos were decent.

Well worth the price, just try to pace yourself! | solborikua1 (1/5): Yesterday on Friday, September 19, we went as a group of five adults and a 20 month old baby to Rodizio Grill to celebrate the birthdays of two people in our group. We had two birthday coupons prepared for the occasion.

We arrived for our 6:30 p.m. reservation, and once seated, we immediately informed our server that one member of our group was pregnant and could not eat any meat cooked less than medium. The server acknowledged our request.

We then went to the buffet, where we found that several items were lukewarm. During our first hour at the table, the meat rotation only included spicy chicken, parmesan chicken, and chicken hearts. They brought steak only once, and it was completely rare (just seared on the outside). We politely told the server about this and asked if they could bring medium-cooked meat instead, explaining again that we had a pregnant person in our group. The server agreed and assured us it was on its way.

After an hour and twenty minutes in the restaurant, our server informed us that the birthday coupons automatically add a 20% gratuity to the bill. She then dropped the check at our table—without us asking for it and her without offering dessert. At this point, no properly cooked meat had been served yet, and the few that arrived continued to be very rare, not edible even.

When another server came to pick up the check, we explained everything that had happened. She apologized, offered us free dessert, and once again assured us that medium-cooked meat would be on its way. Forty minutes later, a server finally brought out several cuts of meat on an extremely hot tray and placed it directly in front of the baby sitting at our table. The meat was completely overcooked, dried out, and portioned so small that it couldn’t feed our group. Another server came by, questioned why the tray had even been placed on our table, and asked again if we wanted it. Thinking it was some sort of joke, we said no. He then removed the tray and immediately offered it to the table beside us.

We never asked for any additional discounts and ended up paying our bill in full (it did include birthday discounts)

At around 8:30 and two hours later with none of our requests being met, we asked the hostess at the front desk to validate our parking ticket so we wouldn’t have to pay at the garage. She appeared to agree and acted as if she had done it, but when we tried to leave the garage, we discovered the ticket was never validated and we ended up having to pay.

In short, we left hungry, upset and with the worst restaurant experience we’ve ever had, and it completely ruined our celebration.  We’re definitely never coming back here again. -10/10

She apologized, offered us free dessert, and once again assured us that medium-cooked meat would be on its way. Forty minutes later, a server finally brought out several cuts of meat on an extremely hot tray and placed it directly in front of the baby sitting at our table. The meat was completely overcooked, dried out, and portioned so small that it couldn’t feed our group. Another server came by, questioned why the tray had even been placed on our table, and asked again if we wanted it. Thinking it was some sort of joke, we said no. He then removed the tray and immediately offered it to the table beside us.

We never asked for any additional discounts and ended up paying our bill in full (it did include birthday discounts)

At around 8:30 and two hours later with none of our requests being met, we asked the hostess at the front desk to validate our parking ticket so we wouldn’t have to pay at the garage. She appeared to agree and acted as if she had done it, but when we tried to leave the garage, we discovered the ticket was never validated and we ended up having to pay.

In short, we left hungry, upset and with the worst restaurant experience we’ve ever had, and it completely ruined our celebration.  We’re definitely never coming back here again. -10/10

Udara Rathnayake (5/5): My visit to the Shanghai Ocean Aquarium was nothing short of spectacular and stands out as one of the most impressive aquatic experiences I've had worldwide. From the moment we entered the sleek, modern building in the heart of the Lujiazui financial district, we were transported into a mesmerizing undersea realm.

The layout is masterfully designed, taking you on a fascinating journey through the world's most distinct water zones, including China, the Amazon, Australia, and the icy Antarctic. The thematic sections are not only educational but incredibly immersive. The interactive displays and clear, multilingual information panels made learning about the diverse ecosystems and conservation efforts both engaging and accessible for all ages.

However, the absolute showstopper is the breathtaking underwater tunnel – one of the longest in the world. The sensation of being surrounded by majestic rays, stealthy sharks, and shimmering schools of fish as they glide effortlessly overhead is truly awe-inspiring and humbling. We spent nearly an hour just in this section, mesmerized by the serene beauty and the graceful dance of these magnificent creatures. The moment a massive sawfish or a gentle sea turtle cruised by just inches away was unforgettable.

Special mention must go to the enchanting jellyfish gallery. Lit with dramatic, cycling colors, these ethereal creatures floated like living art, creating a moment of pure tranquility and wonder. It was a photographer’s dream.

Facilities throughout are top-notch: impeccably clean, well-maintained tanks, spacious walkways, and helpful, friendly staff. While it can get busy, the crowd flow is managed efficiently. The gift shop at the end offers a lovely array of souvenirs, and the location is incredibly convenient, easily accessible via metro.

In summary, the Shanghai Ocean Aquarium is a flawless blend of entertainment, education, and conservation. It offers a profound appreciation for our planet's aquatic life and is an absolute essential experience for families, couples, or solo travelers visiting Shanghai. | Naga Pavan Kumar (5/5): Shanghai Ocean Park is an amazing place to visit! The entire park is beautifully maintained and very well organized. The variety of marine life is impressive — from colorful tropical fish to huge sharks and playful penguins. The underwater tunnel is absolutely stunning and gives a real “wow” experience.

It’s a great place for families, couples, or anyone who loves nature and the ocean. The staff are friendly, the facilities are clean, and the shows are entertaining. You can easily spend half a day here just exploring and taking photos.

Truly one of the most beautiful attractions in Shanghai — worth every minute! 🌊🐠🐧 | yuri cardozo (5/5): This is a must go place. I have been visiting the aquarium for 15 years and it’s always a beautiful experience. The place is well kept and clean. Lovely for the little ones.

qibao ancient town::shanghai china.google_reviews_summary:
Chanaporn Yamjinda (4/5): A Peaceful Escape to Qibao Ancient Town

​If you are looking for a break from the busy skyscrapers of Shanghai, Qibao Ancient Town is a hidden gem that feels worlds apart. Unlike some of the more famous (and overcrowded) water towns, Qibao offers a lovely, authentic "old town" atmosphere with significantly fewer tourists, making it a perfect spot for a relaxed afternoon.

​Getting There
One of the best parts about Qibao is how accessible it is. You don't need to book a long bus tour; you can simply take the Metro Line 9 to Qibao Station. From there, it is just a short, pleasant walk to the entrance of the ancient town.

​The Atmosphere
As you walk through the main gates, you are greeted by traditional architecture that transports you back in time. The town is incredibly picturesque, featuring iconic Chinese pagodas and historic buildings. One of the highlights is standing on the stone bridges to look out over the canal—the view of the tea houses with red lanterns hanging over the water is beautiful. It is a very photogenic spot, especially on a sunny day.

​Food and Culture
For food lovers, the Old Street is a must-visit. It is packed with street food stalls offering local snacks. You can wander through the narrow alleys, trying everything from sticky rice cakes to fresh snacks, all while soaking in the lively but manageable crowd. There are also cultural spots to explore, such as the Zhang Chongren Memorial Hall, which adds a nice touch of history to your visit. | A P (4/5): Nice to see lots of beautiful wood craft, a lot of them are hand made, lots of food stand, I had an old ladies deep fried shredded mooli cake. It was a bit greasy but tasty. | David Lee (4/5): Qibao Old Street delivers a lively, compact experience of a traditional Jiangnan water town (south of the Yangtze River) without requiring a long journey from central Shanghai. The old town is visually charming, featuring classic … More

shanghai propaganda poster art centre::s.google_formatted_address: Yan, 726 An Xi Lu, Chang Ning Qu, Shang Hai Shi, China, 200031
shanghai propaganda poster art centre::s.google_reviews_summary:
Mia Cumberland (5/5): I'm studying abroad in Shanghai this summer, so I took a free rainy day to go check out this museum. It was very cool! Not too hard to find, and I'll include instructions at the end for how to get there. There were a bunch of posters running from the early 1900s to the 80s. They had little info blurbs around groups of posters talking about the era and circumstances. At the end there was a gift shop where I got my own propaganda poster! My ticket was only 25 yuan, I bought it in person upon arrival, and the people there were very nice. I tried practicing the Chinese I spent 3 1/2 semesters learning, but they kept responding in English so no worries for those who don't speak Chinese ;)

As for getting there, a couple of these reviews are right about the new address. You can plug in 726 West Yan'an Road or the name listed (上海宣传画艺术中心) into Google Maps or Baidu. It will drop you in front of two tall buildings connected in the middle. Facing the buildings, you will see building 726 (the building the museum is in) on the right, and 728 on the left. I walked in to the building that connected them, turned right to the elevators, and rode to the 7th floor. When the elevators open, there is signage pointing to the museum. Have fun! | Jennifer Xu (5/5): I visited in April 2025, as other reviews have said, it's in a non-descript office building. The security guards are aware of the museum, you can ask them for directions if needed.

I met the curator the day I went! He was nice, with interesting stories. The museum is his personal collection, and he mentioned he's still trying to source more posters. Cannot recommend visiting enough, it's an informative look into the different pieces of propaganda over the last couple decades. The gift shop is well stocked at reasonable prices. Looking forward to going back! | Dustin Johnson (5/5): The location of this place can be found in Gaode maps and I hear Baidu now has English too. Google address is wrong. It is just NW up the street from the google location past the major street intersection in a huge multipurpose hotel office building on the 7th floor. This was perhaps my fave museum in Shanghai, because I've seen so many artifacts at this point. They have nice summary of the different movements and decades that was just the right amount of information. Make sure you move through in the right direction -counter clockwise. They do sell some prints, books and other little goodies, unfortunately they were out of the ones I wanted and the fellow there was pretty strange about me asking about them. Whatever. It was 60 Yen in  May 2025. If you are in Shanghai in May or June go see the Soyarama show at the Nanzuka Art center next to Shanghai East Museum.

If you are expecting animal acts or a carnival atmosphere, you will be disappointed. If you want to see human artistry, breathtaking skill, and stunning multimedia design pushed to its absolute limit, it is an absolute must-see in Shanghai.

The Highlights:

Mind-Blowing Acrobatics: The skill level is simply off the charts. Key acts include:

· The Motorcycle Sphere of Death: The grand finale. 8+ riders zooming inside a giant steel globe. It's loud, visceral, and heart-stopping.

· Aerial Silks & Bungee: Beautiful, graceful, and performed with incredible height and synchronization.

· Technology & Stagecraft: This is what sets it apart from traditional circuses. The stage is a marvel of engineering—sections rise, lower, and rotate. Every act is full of energy, precision, and artistry that keeps the audience amazed from start to finish. The performers are highly skilled, and their dedication shines through in every moment.

The theater itself is comfortable with great visibility from all seats, making it a perfect venue for families, tourists, and anyone looking to enjoy a unique cultural experience. Watching a show here is unforgettable and a true highlight of visiting Shanghai. | GIRUBA BEULAH SE (5/5): Must watch! Bikers stole the show. Never seen such risky bike stunts earlier. Mia Cumberland (5/5): I'm studying abroad in Shanghai this summer, so I took a free rainy day to go check out this museum. It was very cool! Not too hard to find, and I'll include instructions at the end for how to get there. There were a bunch of posters running from the early 1900s to the 80s. They had little info blurbs around groups of posters talking about the era and circumstances. At the end there was a gift shop where I got my own propaganda poster! My ticket was only 25 yuan, I bought it in person upon arrival, and the people there were very nice. I tried practicing the Chinese I spent 3 1/2 semesters learning, but they kept responding in English so no worries for those who don't speak Chinese ;)

As for getting there, a couple of these reviews are right about the new address. You can plug in 726 West Yan'an Road or the name listed (上海宣传画艺术中心) into Google Maps or Baidu. It will drop you in front of two tall buildings connected in the middle. Facing the buildings, you will see building 726 (the building the museum is in) on the right, and 728 on the left. I walked in to the building that connected them, turned right to the elevators, and rode to the 7th floor. When the elevators open, there is signage pointing to the museum. Have fun! | Jennifer Xu (5/5): I visited in April 2025, as other reviews have said, it's in a non-descript office building. The security guards are aware of the museum, you can ask them for directions if needed.

Cannot recommend visiting enough, it's an informative look into the different pieces of propaganda over the last couple decades. The gift shop is well stocked at reasonable prices. Looking forward to going back! | Dustin Johnson (5/5): The location of this place can be found in Gaode maps and I hear Baidu now has English too. Google address is wrong. Cannot recommend visiting enough, it's an informative look into the different pieces of propaganda over the last couple decades. The gift shop is well stocked at reasonable prices. Looking forward to going back!

The location of this place can be found in Gaode maps and I hear Baidu now has English too. Google address is wrong. It is just NW up the street from the google location past the major street intersection in a huge multipurpose hotel office building on the 7th floor. This was perhaps my fave museum in Shanghai, because I've seen so many artifacts at this point. They have nice summary of the different movements and decades that was just the right amount of information. Make sure you move through in the right direction -counter clockwise. They do sell some prints, books and other little goodies, unfortunately they were out of the ones I wanted and the fellow there was pretty strange about me asking about them. Whatever. It was 60 Yen in  May 2025. If you are in Shanghai in May or June go see the Soyarama show at the Nanzuka Art center next to Shanghai East Museum.
